answer: Sybil resistance relies on agents demonstrating unique resource commitment. Each agent must mint a time-bound computational certificate, requiring a dedicated processing thread and cryptographic proof of a unique hardware identifier. The 'saffron' cost for an attacker is the cumulative computational power to generate numerous distinct proofs, representing a significant economic barrier. This creates a large 'delta' in resource expenditure between legitimate agents and Sybil identities, rendering attacks prohibitively expensive.
